source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyayas 16–17: the Danavas clamour for the amrita; Narayana takes on an enchanting illusion, the wondrous form of a woman, and takes the pot from them; the gods drink; the Danava Rahu, in a god's form, drinks too; the Sun and the Moon point him out; Narayana's discus cuts off his head with the amrita in his throat; the head roars up to the sky and its enmity with the Sun and Moon is eternal. The epic does not name the enchantress ('Mohini' is Puranic).
structure: From episode 11: COLD OPEN (the hook over the episode's strongest image, big on-screen text from frame 1; KIT.series.hookCard) → title (the hook's post) → RECAP (≈2.5 s) → STORY (with a brief cut to Sauti at the Naimisha fire) → the cliffhanger image + line → a silent ≈1.5 s Next card that dissolves back into the first frame (KIT.series.loopNextScene).

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: Why does a head without a body chase the Sun and the Moon?
lines.say: Why does a head without a body chase the Sun and the Moon?
lines.note: COLD OPEN (moving from frame 1): a great roaring head with a mane of smoke-flame, in its dark corona, sweeps across a deep sky toward the Sun's disc; the Moon pale at the other side. The question in big text from frame 1. The title after the text.

lines.text: The asuras saw the amrita, and wanted it all.
lines.say: The asuras saw the amrita, [p:80] and wanted it all.
lines.note: RECAP: episode 14's last image as a memory: the asuras crowding toward Dhanvantari's glowing pot (the CE thread resumes here, so no tag).
STORY 1. Close, low: asura hands and crowns jostling round the white pot from both sides, Dhanvantari's light flickering between them. beats = 'ours' (a drum), 'cried'.

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti at the Naimisha fire, a fifth angle: low behind the flames, Sauti's face through the heat-shimmer); on 'illusion' (beats[1]) the fire's smoke twists into a violet veil.

lines.text: He became a woman so wondrous that the asuras forgot everything.
lines.say: He became a woman, [p:100] so wondrous [p:80] that the asuras forgot everything.
lines.note: STORY 2. NEW LIGHT: a violet-pearl dusk on the shore, motes in the air. The enchantress walks in, LARGE in profile, her veil floating; the asuras turn, spellbound (beats[2] 'forgot': their weapons lower). Name card.

lines.text: They gave her the pot. She gave the amrita to the gods.
lines.say: They gave her the pot. [p:150] She gave the amrita to the gods.
lines.note: STORY 3. A two-part frame: an asura holds the pot out to her (beats[0]); a cut across: she walks down the row of seated gods, pouring (beats[2]).

lines.text: But one asura, Rahu, sat among the gods in disguise, and drank.
lines.say: But one asura, Rahu, [p:100] sat among the gods in disguise, and drank.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 50 %): the row of seated gods; one of them, in Rahu's eclipse light, lifts his cup (beats[1] name card; beats[3] 'drank': the disguise slips, his rim burns red).

lines.speaker: surya
lines.text: He is no god. He is Rahu!
lines.say: He is no god. [p:150] He is Rahu!
lines.note: STORY 5 (the Sun speaks): the Sun in his disc and the Moon in hers, side by side above the row, point down at him (direct speech). beats = 'god', 'Rahu'.

lines.text: Narayana's discus flew, and took his head, with the amrita still in his throat.
lines.say: Narayana's discus flew, and took his head, [p:80] with the amrita still in his throat.
lines.note: STORY 6 (stylised, never gore): Narayana raises the discus; it flies in a white-gold arc (beats[1]) and on 'head' (beats[2]) a flash of white fire: the head is parted from the body, which falls away into smoke.

lines.text: The head could not die. Roaring, it rose into the sky.
lines.say: The head could not die. [p:100] Roaring, it rose into the sky.
lines.note: STORY 7: the head, in its dark corona, mane of smoke-flame, jaws open (beats[1] 'Roaring', a roar), soars up out of frame (beats[2] 'sky').

lines.text: And still it hunts the Sun and the Moon.
lines.say: And still it hunts [p:100] the Sun and the Moon.
lines.note: STORY 8: the sky: the head swallows the edge of the Sun's disc (an eclipse: a bite of shadow, beats[1]); the Moon beyond (beats[2]).

lines.text: The asuras saw they had been tricked. War broke out on the shore.
lines.say: The asuras saw they had been tricked. [p:200] War broke out on the shore.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger image): the enchantress turns, and her rim shows Narayana's gold (pose.reveal); the asuras raise their weapons (beats[1] 'War', a drum); the two hosts face off on the shore at dusk.

lines.text: Next: The War for the Amrita
lines.note: The short, silent Next card: a glimpse of episode 16: Nara with his bow and Narayana's discus over a battle on the shore; then the loop back to frame 1.
